_comment: Per-string context pushed to Crowdin by `npm run i18n:context`. One line per key saying where the string appears and what constrains it — the facts a translator cannot get from the English alone. Written when the string is, by whoever ran /wording. Keys mirror en.json.
pattern: Assembles the alias shown to an anonymous account in Settings -> Account, e.g. "Forgetful Professor". Word order is yours to change; keep both params. The panel gives the name as much room as it needs and lets it wrap, so length is not a constraint - do not shorten a natural rendering to save characters.
quirk.1: Adjective pool for the drawn alias (30 entries). Each entry pairs with every one of the 26 `archetype` nouns, so it must work with all of them: if your language marks gender, translate the whole `archetype` pool in a single gender and write this pool to agree with that one gender throughout. It is a trait of the fictional character the alias names, never a judgement of the player. One word per entry; no length limit.
quirk.2: Adjective pool for the drawn alias; pairs with all 26 `archetype` nouns - see `quirk.1` for the gender rule. No length limit.

archetype.1: Noun pool for the drawn alias (26 entries) - the kinds of person these stories are about, which is why it uses story vocabulary rather than the archive vocabulary of the surrounding screen. Each entry pairs with every one of the 30 `quirk` adjectives. Keep the whole pool in one grammatical gender so the adjectives can agree, and keep every entry usable for a player of any gender: if a natural translation of an entry presupposes a woman or a man, choose a different archetype instead. One word per entry; no length limit.
